<!-- # Lightning.ai Account - Setup Instructions -->

---


## 1. Set up Lightning.ai Account

-  Go to: <https://lightning.ai/pricing/>
-  Click on **Get started free**
-  Select **Email** (first option), then type in your **university email address**
-  You will then receive an email to confirm your email address. Click on the **Log in** button in that email, which will take you back to their website. Then click **Next**
-  On the next page (`How do you want to code:`), click on **Browser**, and click **Next**
-  On the following page (`What machine do you want to use:`), click on **CPU** (top left option), and click **Next**
-  On the next page, enter your mobile phone number (this is being used for two-factor authentication), and click on **Request verification code**
-  You will be sent a 6-digit code by text message (SMS). Enter this code where it says **Enter verification code**. Then click **Verify**
-  When you see `Congratulations, your account is verified!`: Click **Next**
-  Then you see `Invite members (optional)`: Click **Next**
-  For `Select Git integration:`: Choose **Connect later** (right-hand option), and click **Next**, then click **Start building!**
-  When you see `Welcome to your first Studio ...`: Click **Next**
-  When you see `You are on the Free tier ...`: Click **I understand**.
-  You are now in the first **Studio** created on Lightning.ai. On the right-hand side, Lightning.ai's _native credit-consuming **AI copilot** service_ is enabled by default. You can try if you like it. (Clicking the **AI copilot** button near the top right part of the Studio toggles off the services.) 
-  Alternatively, you can follow the instructions below to enable and use the **GitHub Copilot** chat interface

---

(_Note:_ Use of GitHub Copilot on Lightning.ai will _**consumer your GitHub credit allowance**_, not the credit allowance provided by Lightning.ai.)

## 2. Enable GitHub Copilot on Lightning.ai

- In a Lightning.ai Studio, log into your GitHub account using the **'human head' credentials button** in the lower left corner
  - This should be sufficient to enable the GitHub Copilot chat interface in the right-hand side panel
- Once logged in, a window will pop up asking for the permission as follows:

> *The extension 'GitHub Copilot Chat' wants to sign in using GitHub.*  
> *To show you more relevant Copilot Chat results, we need permission to read the contents of your repository on GitHub.*

- Click the **Allow** button. Then follow the additional instructions on screen to complete the process
- When completed, click the **Toggle Secondary Side Bar** button in the upper right corner to toggle on the panel with the GitHub Copilot chat interface.
- If the GitHub Copilot chat interface does not already allow you to select the **Mode** (Ask/Plan/Agent) from a drop-down menu, enter a trivial question like '**hi there**'
  - This should initialize the default AI model and give you a reply like ‘*What can I help you today?*’. The Mode selector should then be available for selection

---

(*Note*: Teamspace is now called **Organization**)

## 3. Create a Studio in a Teamspace

- Each Studio must belong to a Teamspace, where users can be invited to collaborate on Studios in the Teamspace. 
  - Even for an individual user, one must select an existing/set up a new Teamspace before a Studio can be created in it 
- If you are currently inside a Studio, you can shut it down first, which will take you to the **Dashboard** page showing all your Teamspaces and the Studios in each Teamspace
  - To shut down a Studio when you are in it, click the **CPU button** (or **T4** button) near the top right corner of the Studio, followed by clicking the green **Power** button on the top line of the pop-up window
  - Then click **Yes, sleep** in the next window
- The first time you shut down your first Studio, you will see a pop-up window `This is your Lightning teamspace`. Click **CLOSE** in the upper left corner to close it. This will take you to the Dashboard page
- To create a new Teamspace, click the **‘+’ button** in the lower left corner of the page, followed by clicking the **Next** button to accept the **Default** choice in the pop-up window
  - In the next window, give a **name** to the new Teamspace to be created, followed by clicking the **Create** button
- On the next page, click the ‘**+ New Studio**’ button to create a new Studio in the newly created Teamspace.
  - Select, for example, **Python** in the pop-up window and leave the machine type unchanged (i.e., **Default (CPU)**)
  - Then click the **Start** button. This will complete the steps to create the new Studio
- Be patient to wait until the **progress bar** near the top of the newly created Studio to reach **100%** before doing anything in the Studio 
  - Otherwise, any interruption runs the risk of causing defects in the Studio and unexpected behaviors.
- The (VS Code) interface of a Lightning.ai **Studio** is highly similar to the (VS Code) interface of a **GitHub Cospace**. 
  - Additionally, you can switch to Lightning.ai's **JupyterLab** interface by clicking the respective button on the vertical menu bar at the right edge of the Studio.
- A Studio will get into **Auto sleep after 10 mins of inactivity**, or **after being used continuously for 4 hours**.

---

(*Note*: Below is for use _**during the Workshop**_)

## 4. Clone a Studio shared through a Studio template

- Click the link **BigramCloud_GPUorCPU** provided in the Workshop slides, which will take you to a page with a **Clone button**. 
  - Click the button to clone the Studio to your Lightning.ai account.
- In the pop-up window, _**select the Teamspace**_ where you would like to clone the Studio, followed by clicking **Open**.
- Because the default machine of the shared Studio is **T4**, you must have credits in the selected Teamspace (or transfer some into it) before the shared Studio can be cloned there.
  - Click the **Transfer credits** link in the pop-up window to transfer in credits (if there is no credit in the chosen Teamspace). Then click the **Confirm** button to confirm the transfer.
- Click **Open** to open the cloned Studio.
  - If the value of the transferred-in credits is regarded low, you will see a pop-up window to suggest **Add credits**. You can remove the window by clicking the **‘x’ button**.
